title: Session cache: Redis vs Valkey
brief: The same session cache as in Redis vs Memcached: 50k requests/s, 95% reads, 3 cache nodes with AOF persistence and a replica each. Side A runs Redis, side B runs Valkey, the open-source fork of Redis. Run the scenarios, then decide what actually separates them.

scenarios.label: Steady 50k rps
scenarios.about: Nothing fails. Look at the cost and memory rows.

scenarios.label: Restart the cache
scenarios.about: At 10 s the cache restarts (down for 2 s). Both reload their keys from AOF.

questions: The sim runs both the same way. Which row differs, and by how much per year for this cluster?

Redis moved from BSD to RSALv2/SSPLv1 in March 2024 (from 7.4) and added AGPLv3 as an option from Redis 8. Valkey continued from the BSD code as a Linux Foundation project. Does either license matter if you only use a managed service? If you embed or resell it?
Valkey speaks the same protocol. What would you test before switching a production cache?
What would keep you on Redis: newer Redis-only features, a support contract, something else?
hints: Compare the two columns row by row. Which ones are equal?
Only price differs here. Multiply the cost gap per hour by 8,760 hours.

Valkey saves about $0.044 per node-hour on ElastiCache: about $2,300 a year for 6 nodes (3 plus replicas). The rest is license and roadmap: who you buy from, which features you need, and how much testing a swap takes.
_notes: Graph: session-cache.json (see redis-vs-memcached). Valkey preset: same cache handler and params as Redis; capacity kept equal (estimate); ElastiCache cache.r7g.large $0.1752 vs $0.219/node-hr. 3 nodes x 2 (replica): $1.31 vs $1.05/hr for the cache, about $2,300/yr. Sim: identical p99 (61 ms steady, 111 ms restart), errors (3.4% in the restart), recovery (2.5 s) and hit; only cost ($3.91 vs $3.65/hr total) and memory cost per GB ($0.034 vs $0.027/GB-hr) differ. License facts: redis.io/legal/licenses (March 2024 RSALv2/SSPLv1 from 7.4; 7.2.x stays BSD3; AGPLv3 option from Redis 8, redis.io/blog/agplv3), valkey.io/topics/history (fork of open-source Redis under BSD, Linux Foundation project, announced 8 days after the license change). Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
